script:
Hey guys, let's talk AI. Did you know that the first AI program was created in 1951 by Alan Turing? He wanted to see if machines could think like humans.

Fast forward to today and AI is everywhere. From your phone to your fridge, there's an AI algorithm running in the background making it all work.

But did you know that most AI systems are trained on data from just a few hundred thousand examples? That's it. A tiny fraction of the data we use every day.

And get this - some AI models can recognize faces with 99% accuracy, but they still can't recognize humor or sarcasm. Talk about irony.

AI is also getting more and more autonomous. Imagine your home assistant suddenly deciding to take control of your entire life without you knowing what's going on.

It's wild to think that AI has been around for over 70 years, yet we're only just starting to scratch the surface of its potential. What does this mean for our future?
